items.title: Meloni calls Trump tariffs a 'mistake,' proposes EU-US free-trade zone

featured_image.name: Italy's PM Meloni calls Trump's Greenland tariffs on Europe a mistake

items.description:
In an interview with Bloomberg published Friday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called for the European Union to form a free-trade zone with the United States, an ambitious proposal aimed at resolving the transatlantic tariff standoff that has rattled markets and stalled trade policy on both sides of the Atlantic.[1][2]

Meloni described President Donald Trump's tariffs as a "mistake" and urged the EU to move forward with adopting the trade agreement it struck with Washington last summer, known as the Turnberry deal, according to Bloomberg. The deal, reached at Trump's Scottish golf resort in July 2025, set a 15% ceiling on tariffs for most EU exports to the United States in exchange for the EU eliminating import duties on all US industrial goods.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Taliban signal willingness to talk after Pakistan launches airstrikes

featured_image.name: Pakistan says ‘patience has run out' as it bombs Taliban across Afghanistan

items.description:
Afghanistan's Taliban government said Friday it was open to negotiations with Pakistan, even as the two nations exchanged their most serious cross-border attacks in years. The diplomatic overture came hours after Pakistan launched airstrikes on Kabul, Kandahar, and Paktia province, with its defense minister declaring that the countries are now in a state of "open war."[1][2][3]

The conflicting signals — a willingness to talk paired with escalating military operations — underscore the volatile and rapidly shifting dynamics between the once-allied neighbors, whose relationship has deteriorated sharply over Pakistan's accusations that the Taliban harbors militant groups responsible for attacks inside Pakistani territory.

items.title: Trump warns of military force against Iran as nuclear talks stall

featured_image.name: Trump's claim on Iranian missile development said ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday expressed frustration with the progress of nuclear negotiations with Iran and warned that military force remains on the table, telling reporters, "Don't want to, but sometimes you have to," when asked whether he would order strikes against the Islamic Republic.[1][2]

Speaking to reporters before departing the White House for a trip to Texas, Trump said he was "not happy" with Iran's posture in the talks and reiterated his core demand. "I'm not happy with the fact that they're not willing to give us what we have to have. I'm not thrilled with that," he said, adding: "Iran cannot have nuclear weapons".[3][4]

items.title: IAEA says Iran stored near-weapons-grade uranium underground

featured_image.name: IAEA chief says Iran could be enriching uranium within ...

items.description:
Some of Iran's most highly enriched uranium was stored in an underground tunnel complex at its nuclear site in Isfahan prior to last year's U.S. strikes, the International Atomic Energy Agency said in a confidential report circulated to member states on Friday, marking the first time the U.N. nuclear watchdog has specified where uranium enriched to up to 60% purity has been kept.[1][2]

The disclosure adds a new dimension to the standoff over Tehran's nuclear program, arriving as the United States and Iran pursue fragile diplomatic negotiations and Washington maintains a large military buildup across the Middle East.

items.title: Green Party wins first-ever UK by-election, pushing Labour to third

featured_image.name: UK Greens trounce far right in key election as Labour fall to ...

items.description: Hannah Spencer, a 34-year-old plumber and local councillor, has won the Gorton and Denton by-election in Greater Manchester, delivering a result that marks the first time in the Green Party's history that it has won a UK parliamentary by-election. The victory, declared in the early hours of Friday morning, saw Spencer capture 14,980 votes — roughly 40.7% of the total — overturning a Labour majority of more than 13,000 from the 2024 general election. The result pushes Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party into third place in a seat the party had held for nearly a century.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: OpenAI raises record $110B from Amazon, Nvidia, SoftBank

featured_image.name: OpenAI said to be finalizing $100 billion funding round

items.description:
OpenAI announced on Friday a $110 billion funding round at a $730 billion pre-money valuation, the largest private financing deal ever recorded. The round includes $50 billion from Amazon, $30 billion from Nvidia, and $30 billion from SoftBank, with additional financial investors expected to join as the round progresses.[1]

The deal cements a sweeping strategic partnership between OpenAI and Amazon and deepens the AI company's ties to its largest chip supplier, Nvidia, while more than doubling the $40 billion OpenAI raised in March 2025 in what was then the biggest private tech fundraise on record.[2]

items.title: Chinese scientists set world records for kesterite, polymer solar cells

featured_image.name: Kesterite solar cells get ready to shine

items.description:
Researchers in China have announced back-to-back breakthroughs in solar cell technology, setting world records for both kesterite and polymer photovoltaic devices in findings published this week.

The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) reported that its Qingdao Institute of Bioenergy and Bioprocess Technology fabricated a kesterite solar cell achieving a power conversion efficiency of 15.45%, with a certified efficiency of 15.04%, according to pv magazine. Separately, a team at Wuhan University of Technology unveiled a polymer solar cell reaching 19.1% efficiency while retaining 97% of its performance after 2,000 hours of operation in air.[1][2]

items.title: Astronomers reveal trio of rare cosmic finds in single week

featured_image.name: Astrophotographers show the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A

items.description: In a burst of discoveries announced over the past week, astronomers using some of the world's most advanced telescopes have revealed three rare and violent cosmic phenomena: the first image of a young Sun-like star inflating a protective bubble in space, possible evidence of an elusive black hole shredding a white dwarf, and the fading radio echo of a powerful explosion whose original blast went unseen.

items.title: Zelenskyy says he's ready to meet Putin for peace talks

featured_image.name: Zelenskyy speaks with Trump about peace efforts, eyes leaders ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he is ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin face-to-face to resolve the most difficult issues standing in the way of peace, while warning that surrendering Ukrainian-held fortress cities in the east remains a firm red line.

In a wide-ranging interview with Sky News published on February 27, Zelenskyy said there is a closing window to end the war — one tied to American domestic politics. "Now I think that we have a chance," he told correspondent Alex Rossi. "If it will be possible to achieve a peace, we will have, now we have this window" — between now and the U.S. midterm elections in November.[1][2]

items.title: Chinese scientists achieve 700 Wh/kg lithium battery breakthrough

featured_image.name: New breakthrough in lithium battery technology enables 700 ...

items.description:
A team of Chinese researchers has developed a novel lithium battery electrolyte system that achieves an energy density of 700 watt-hours per kilogram at room temperature — more than double the capacity of the best commercially available lithium-ion batteries. The findings, published February 25 in Nature, represent a potential leap forward for electric vehicles, aerospace, and cold-weather energy storage.[1][2][3]

The research was led by Professor Zhao Qing from the College of Chemistry at Nankai University, Academician Chen Jun, the university's executive vice president, and Researcher Li Yong from the Shanghai Institute of Space Power-Sources. Their approach replaces the conventional carbonate ester solvents used in commercial lithium battery electrolytes with a series of fluorinated hydrocarbon solvent molecules, establishing a lithium-fluorine coordination system in place of the traditional lithium-oxygen mechanism.[4][2]
